name: Sticky Hoisin "Bat Wings" with Green Onions & Sesame Seeds

instructions.primary_message: Preheat oven to 450°F. Line a large baking sheet pan with aluminum foil to make cleanup easier; coat with a thin layer of oil.
Pat chicken wings dry with paper towels and place in a large bowl. Sprinkle with cornstarch, salt, and pepper, then toss to coat. Transfer to the baking sheet and arrange in a single layer.
instructions.secondary_message:
4 ½ lb chicken wings, whole
2 tbsp cornstarch
1 tsp salt
½ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Place baking sheet in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and bake, turning once, until wings are golden and partially cooked through, 20-25 minutes.
Meanwhile, place hoisin sauce and honey in a small saucepan. Stir to combine the glaze.
instructions.secondary_message:
½ cup hoisin sauce
¼ cup honey

instructions.primary_message: Set saucepan over medium-high heat and bring to a simmer. Once simmering, reduce heat to low and cook, stirring occasionally, until glaze reduces by one-third, 4-5 minutes. Remove from heat and cover to keep warm.
When the wings are golden, remove from the oven. Drizzle half of the glaze over the wings, turning them to coat. (Reserve remaining glaze for later use.)
Return baking sheet to the oven and continue to bake until wings are sticky, dark golden brown, and cooked through, 8-10 minutes more.
Meanwhile, wash, dry, trim, and cut green onions crosswise into thin pieces.
When the wings are done, remove from the oven. Drizzle with remaining glaze and turn to coat. (Alternatively, you can use a pastry brush to coat the wings with the glaze.)
Transfer sticky "bat wings" to a platter, then sprinkle with green onions and sesame seeds. Enjoy!
